outlier.evidence: 3 against 7 (Reviewer_gFL6) and 6 (Reviewer_e4YX). The objection is specific and checkable: a barycenter with n support points is an n-clustering of the pooled input points under extra coupling constraints, and MMR19 preserves the cost of every n-clustering, so it implies Theorem 4.1. W1WL wrote the reduction out in the comment of 2021-08-10. The authors conceded it on 2021-08-10 and 2021-08-12. The submission's Definition 2.2 and line 174 confirm the clustering form of the cost. W1WL credited the other results as 'interesting' and objected to the framing, not to correctness.

checkable_claims.claim: [MMR19] directly implies Theorem 4.1: the barycenter problem with support n is an n-clustering of the pooled multiset with coupling constraints, and MMR preserves the cost of every n-clustering, so it preserves every constrained one.
checkable_claims.evidence: Definition 2.2 defines cost_p(S) as the minimum over centres of (1/k) times the sum over j and x in S_j of w_j(x)||x - nu_j||^p, a weighted n-clustering cost; line 174 calls each term 'just a weighted k-means problem'. Theorem 4.1 (lines 241-243) holds 'for all solutions S', as MMR holds for all clusterings, and its dimension does not depend on the number or size of the input distributions. The authors (2021-08-10) said the proof of Theorem 4.1 already takes the multiset view and 'the discretization does not affect the assumptions required for the dimensionality reduction maps'; on 2021-08-12 they promised to add 'the elegant connection between [MMR] and one of our theorems'. The camera-ready deletes the paragraph (submission lines 261-278) listing four difficulties beyond MMR, which the rebuttal had cited as the novelty.

checkable_claims.claim: The assumption that each input distribution has support poly(n) seems unnecessary; only the barycenter support size n matters.
checkable_claims.evidence: Through the conceded reduction, the MMR dimension depends on the number of clusters, not on the number of points. The rebuttal recast the assumption as a modelling choice and named no proof step that needs it.

checkable_claims.claim: On MNIST the reduced-dimension run takes 73% of the full-dimension time, against 9% on FACES.
checkable_claims.evidence: Lines 354-355 give 73% and 9%. gFL6 asked twice for the MNIST per-step breakdown; the authors gave a sparsity guess, then FACES timings only (0.02 s projection, 0.43 s solver, 0.17 s reconstruction, against 7.81 s).

checkable_claims.claim: The coreset comparison with uniform sampling gives only numbers, with no graphs and no variance.
checkable_claims.evidence: Figure 3 (page 9) is a table of mean percentage errors over 10 repetitions with no spread. The camera-ready keeps the same table.

checkable_claims.claim: The coreset size is O(n^8), from the VC-dimension bound, and so is impractical for large n.
checkable_claims.evidence: The main text states only poly(n, d)/epsilon^2 (Theorem 5.2, line 310); the exponent is in Supplementary Theorem C.9, which is not in the PDF. The authors agreed that the bound is not tight.

rebuttal.evidence: No review was edited after the rebuttal: Reviewer_e4YX's edit is dated 2021-07-15, the day it was posted. Reviewer_W1WL (2021-08-12) found the extra results 'interesting' but wrote that 'the main result (Theorem 1.1) and most of the technical work is a direct corollary of [MMR]' and kept 3. Reviewer_gFL6 (2021-08-11) and Reviewer_e4YX (2021-08-12) posted follow-up requests and did not post again.
rebuttal.what_convinced_or_not: The authors first called barycenters and clustering 'fundamentally different' and cited lines 261-278. W1WL's written reduction answered this, and the authors conceded and promised to add the connection. W1WL accepted the other results as merits but held that the write-up must change before publication. gFL6's MNIST breakdown was answered with FACES numbers. e4YX got timing numbers in text, not the requested graphs.

ac.evidence: Ratings 7, 6, 3 (mean 5.33). The meta-review opens 'As pointed out by the reviewer W1WL ... the main result follows relatively directly from [MMR]' and asks for 'a major rewrite'. It overrides the 7 and the 6, whose reviewers never addressed MMR. Its second point, that 'some reviewers' were not satisfied with the MNIST time breakdown, is right in substance, since the authors answered with FACES; but only Reviewer_gFL6 asked, and gFL6 did not comment on the answer.

verdict: Committee A rejected because Reviewer_W1WL showed that the main result is a corollary of MMR19; Committee B never tested this. Theorem 4.1 says that a JL map to O(log n) dimensions preserves the cost of every barycenter solution with n support points. W1WL wrote the barycenter problem as an n-clustering of the pooled input points with extra coupling constraints; MMR19 preserves the cost of every n-clustering, so it also preserves every constrained one. The submission's Definition 2.2 and line 174 give the cost exactly this clustering form. The authors first called the problems 'fundamentally different', then conceded and promised to add 'the elegant connection between [MMR] and one of our theorems'. The camera-ready deletes the paragraph (submission lines 261-278) that claimed four new difficulties beyond MMR. A's AC made this decisive against the 7 and 6 of two reviewers who never addressed MMR, and added that the authors answered the MNIST timing question with FACES numbers. B's four reviewers took the dimensionality reduction as the paper's main strength ('quite strong', 'impressive'); only Reviewer_1Zyc mentioned MMR19, as a foundation. B's criticisms were thin experiments and presentation, which both committees saw and neither treated as fatal. The decisive fact reached only A, so this is not the same facts weighted differently. The paper keeps real results beyond Theorem 4.1 (coresets, NP-hardness, lower bounds), and the program chairs accepted on B's recommendation.
